solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Truly, trouble dogs a South American absent from work

indicators.note: to dog someone is to follow at their heels, so the trouble word comes after the opening letters

parts.note: 'What's the matter?' asks what the trouble is
someone off work is absent from it
an act is a piece of work or a deed

explanation.surface: Some misfortune follows a South American who has skipped work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word joining OFF (absent) to ACT (work).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to stress that something is really so, matching 'truly' as an adverb of emphasis.

clue.text: Makes free pack up to represent English in Masters

indicators.note: one thing standing in to represent another takes its place, so a swap is made

parts.note: aces are experts, masters of their craft
to pack up a job is to quit it

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a team representing England at the Masters golf tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to represent English in' says QUIT takes the place of the E in ACES.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that acquits a defendant releases them, declaring them not guilty.

clue.text: Element of the USA like president that's retired but not old

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the manner of, like

indicators.note: 'but not' tells the solver to leave the following letter out of the president's name

parts.note: Barack Obama is a former, retired US president

explanation.surface: Part of the USA is likened to a president who has stepped down but isn't elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: BAMA is OBAMA without its O; ALA is the French borrowing 'a la'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty states making up the USA, so a component of it.

clue.text: For example, if used in broadcast it makes a better atmosphere

indicators.note: something used in another is put inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: an airing is a broadcast of a programme
the word if introduces a condition, so if is an example of one

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how the word if is used on air to make a broadcast more pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' is the container signal; 'if' stands for the grammatical idea it introduces, and 'broadcast' is the noun sense, a programme going out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooling and cleaning the air indoors makes a room's atmosphere more comfortable.

clue.text: Act as secretary, chuck in pigeonhole

parts.note: a secretary's work is to type letters
to chuck something is to cast or throw it

explanation.surface: An office worker told to act as a secretary and throw things into the filing slots.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole someone is to stereotype them in one fixed role, as an actor may be.

clue.text: Take too much in payment for unwelcome house guest?

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, inside the payment word

parts.note: rent is the payment a tenant makes
OD is short for overdose, to take too much of a drug

explanation.surface: A landlord overcharging rent to a lodger who has outstayed their welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'guest' is a mouse or rat living uninvited in a house, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice and rats invade homes uninvited, making them unwanted lodgers in a playful sense.

clue.text: My clients are late

parts.note: late here means deceased, not behind time; the speaker serves the dead

explanation.surface: A professional grumbling that customers never arrive on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' reads as tardy but means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker arranges burials for people who have died, the 'late' as clients.

clue.text: Flowing chorus after tune getting this person a bit down

indicators.note: the chorus word comes after the tune in the answer

indicators.text: getting this person a bit down
indicators.note: this person is the setter, I, whose letter shifts a little way down the column

parts.note: an air is a tune
to chorus is to sing together

explanation.surface: Someone feels low as a flowing chorus follows a melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting this person a bit down' shifts the setter's I one place later in the tune word, down the column in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream arising from a source issues or emanates from it, as flowing water does.

clue.text: Buying a suit thus one does push one's luck

definitions.text: Buying a suit thus one does
definitions.meaning: before buying a suit you put it on to test the fit
to chance it, testing how much one can get away with

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both test clothing by wearing it and chance a cheeky attempt at deception.

clue.text: Standing symmetrically, four-foot one

parts.note: a four-footed creature stands evenly on two pairs of legs, balanced on both sides

explanation.surface: A description of something four feet tall standing evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four-foot' suggests a height but means having four feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Any animal walking on four legs, such as a horse or dog, is this kind of creature.

clue.text: Those old revolutionary guards one's blasting

indicators.note: the outer word guards the inner one by surrounding it
revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: yon is an old word for those
one's is read as one is, I + S

explanation.surface: Old revolutionary guards are making a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns YON into NOY, which 'guards' IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is blasting out is loud, making a lot of din.

clue.text: 'State of the Union' part offered by Tarantino had Ice-T heading west

indicators.note: heading west says the hidden letters are read backwards
a part offered by these words is a run of letters taken from inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A film director gave a rapper a role in a film called State of the Union.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'part offered' into the definition; it is the hidden-word signal, and the definition is just 'State of the Union'. Read westward, OHADI gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the states of the American Union, playing on the President's annual speech.

clue.text: Bacon for one, of course not cold, knocked back before shark

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed before the painter word
knocked back means turned back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: of course not! is an emphatic no
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Francis Bacon was a famous painter, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is turned down by a school, ahead of a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns NO + C into CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A shark is a swindler, someone who cheats people out of money.

clue.text: It's essential for celebrity kiss-and-tellers perhaps to come over clean

indicators.note: coming over means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: people who betray secrets are rats, kiss-and-tellers being one example
to dust is to clean

explanation.surface: Famous people need those who sell their stories to come clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come over' turns RATS into STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The magical glamour attached to fame is the quality that makes a famous person shine.

clue.text: 'Goal's rigged,' 15 chant

indicators.note: a rigged result has been fixed or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 15-down answer is the gas whose chemical symbol is N

explanation.surface: Football fans chanting that a goal was fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' rearranges GOALS into SLOGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchphrase, often repeated aloud by a crowd or campaign.

clue.text: News about violent riot, say — uplifting, atmospheric stuff

indicators.note: the outer letters go about, around, the rest

parts.note: N stands for new, so news gives two of them

indicators.note: violent signals the letters of riot thrown into disorder
in a down clue, uplifting means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A news report about a violent riot ends on an uplifting, atmospheric note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' makes ITRO from RIOT; 'uplifting' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas makes up about four-fifths of the air, the main substance of the atmosphere.

clue.text: British in origin, southern individuals that are power-driven?

indicators.note: the letter goes in the origin word

parts.note: a root is the origin of something

explanation.surface: People of British descent from the south who are ambitious for power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power-driven' sounds like ambition but means run by electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Machines that work automatically by electric power can act like mechanical people.

clue.text: Mandarin's refined in this Maoist record

parts.note: red is the colour of communism, so a Maoist is a red
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: A Chinese speaker polishes their language in a record of Mao's thought.
explanation.walkthrough: A mandarin here is a senior civil servant, not the Chinese language: bureaucracy is their refined art.
explanation.definitionFit: Bureaucratic paperwork and procedure is the world in which a senior civil servant excels.

clue.text: Road movies actor must suppress food craving

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so the food goes inside

parts.note: Bing Crosby starred with Bob Hope in the Road to ... films
an egg is a food

explanation.surface: An actor in road films has to curb his appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: Craving something, a person is pleading for it, desperate to have it.

clue.text: Historic event in which well-mannered turned rough

parts.note: civil means polite, well-mannered

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: raw can mean rough or crude

explanation.surface: A well-behaved occasion that became violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes WAR from RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The English and American internal conflicts are famous episodes in history.

clue.text: Film short service, one that's sacred to enter

indicators.note: the saint's letters enter, going inside the short word

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small or short
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy person
the RN, Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A brief church service in a film, with a holy person coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' means an armed service, not a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy picture set in the American West is a film genre.

clue.text: Places for holidays, rests or ____?

indicators.note: the blank asks for the word meaning rearranges, so filled in it signals the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Holiday spots are where people rest, or do something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing word is the answer itself in its verb sense, sorts again, which makes it the signal that RESTS OR is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside towns and ski centres are holiday destinations people visit.

clue.text: Race developed so small, but not small once

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
but not means leave out the following abbreviation
once says only a single copy is dropped, not both

explanation.surface: A race grew from something tiny that wasn't always small.
explanation.walkthrough: SO SMALL less one S leaves SOMALL, which 'developed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A downhill ski race weaving between gates is a competitive event.

clue.text: Auxiliary money trading starts to be minister's trademark?

indicators.note: the two words trade their starting letters with each other

parts.note: a cog in a machine is a minor, auxiliary part
a dollar is a unit of money

explanation.surface: A deputy trading currency to start a government minister's brand.
explanation.walkthrough: The minister is a clergyman, not a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy wear a white collar band, the distinctive mark of their calling.

clue.text: No place in contents for moderates

indicators.note: no place in means the place abbreviation is not in the word, so it is removed

parts.note: to content someone is to please them
PL is the abbreviation for place on maps

explanation.surface: No room in the table of contents for moderate politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' is a verb, satisfies, not a book's list.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate pain or pressure is to lessen or relieve it.

clue.text: Somewhat glib, I lark around getting legal letter off

indicators.note: around means turned round, so those letters are read backwards
somewhat means only part of the words, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking prankster escaping a solicitor's letter.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'letter off' is a thing that lets you off: a legal let-off, not a written letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere at the time of a crime gets an accused person acquitted.

clue.text: Long stretch of time with part of crossword to fill in

indicators.note: the time word is set alongside, after the crossword word

parts.words: part of crossword to fill in
parts.note: a light is a space in a crossword grid for an answer
a year is a unit of time

explanation.surface: A long period of time spent completing a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long stretch of time' looks like a single definition, but the answer measures distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance light travels in a year, nearly six trillion miles, is a vast span.

clue.text: Symbolic circles made with stones

parts.note: jewelled bands, often set with diamonds, symbolising a promise to marry

explanation.surface: Ancient stone circles with ritual meaning, like Stonehenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The stones are gems, not standing megaliths.
explanation.definitionFit: Rings given when a couple agree to marry are usually set with precious gems.
